summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with a history of psoriatic arthritis, diabetes, morbid obesity, and prior leg abscess was admitted for recurrent left calf swelling and spontaneous sanguinous drainage from a prior incision site. He had erythema, warmth, and ecchymosis but no fever or systemic signs of infection. Initial ultrasound showed a complex fluid collection without DVT. MRI revealed fluid tracking and mild myositis without abscess. Infectious disease recommended against antibiotics given stable vitals, normal labs, and no growth on blood cultures. The patient improved with conservative management, including pain control and continued immunosuppressive therapy. His blood sugars, initially over 400, were managed by increasing basal and prandial insulin. He was discharged home with optimized diabetes regimen, steroid taper adjustments, new antihypertensive, and follow-up planned with rheumatology.
problems: Secondary diabetes mellitus without mention of complication, uncontrolled
